verdicts.title: A Ballistic Monte Carlo Approximation of π
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We compute a Monte Carlo approximation of π using importance sampling with shots coming out of a Mossberg 500 pump-action shotgun as the proposal distribution. An approximated value of 3.131 is obtained, corresponding to a 0.33% error on the exact value of π. To our knowledge, this represents the first attempt at estimating π using such method, thus opening up new perspectives towards computing mathematical constants using everyday tools.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The cited paper estimates the mathematical constant π via Monte Carlo with shotgun pellets — it has no connection to resolution proof complexity, DP elimination, or Tseitin formulas. The shared symbol 'π' is coincidental (the conjecture uses π as a proof/permutation).

verdicts.title: 3-regular matchstick graphs with given girth
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We consider 3-regular planar matchstick graphs, i.e. those which have a planar embedding such that all edge lengths are equal, with given girth g. For girth 3 it is known that such graphs exist if and only if the number of vertices n is an even integer larger or equal to 8. Here we prove that such graphs exist for girth g=4 if and only if n is even and at least 20. We provide an example for girth g=5 consisting of 180 vertices.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns 3-regular planar matchstick graphs with prescribed girth, a combinatorial/geometric graph existence problem, with no connection to DP elimination, resolution proof complexity, or Tseitin formula hardness scaling.

verdicts.title: Error exponents of quantum state discrimination with composite correlated hypotheses
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We study the error exponents in quantum hypothesis testing between two sets of quantum states, extending the analysis beyond the independent and identically distributed case to encompass composite correlated hypotheses.
